attacker.model: claude (Kiro subagent; exact model version not exposed to the agent)

notApplicable.identity-gaps: The only key column is Website.SensorDataList.SensorDataListID, an IDENTITY the harness renumbers 1..n for each call (tvpJson), so a planted gap in it cannot reach either engine; Warehouse.ColdRoomTemperatures has no key the procedure uses.

cases.label: a reading at the maximum datetime2 (9999-12-31) updates every existing row for its sensor
cases.reasoning: A new reading for sensor 1 with RecordedWhen 9999-12-31T23:59:59.999999 updates all existing sensor-1 rows. datetime2(7) holds 100 ns ticks and timestamp holds microseconds, so the boundary value tests that the stored RecordedWhen matches after the mapping.

cases.label: temperature 4.25 is stored exactly; a second reading overflows decimal(10,2) and rolls both back
cases.reasoning: Reading 1 stores 4.25 (ends in 5, exact in decimal(10,2)); reading 2 is 123456789.00 which overflows decimal(10,2). ATOMIC/exception semantics mean both engines raise and leave Warehouse.ColdRoomTemperatures unchanged (reading 1 undone too).

cases.label: three rows for sensor 3 (two equal in every column) are all updated by one reading; rows for sensors 30, 0 and -3 with the same values are left alone
cases.reasoning: The UPDATE ... WHERE ColdRoomSensorNumber = 3 must rewrite every sensor-3 row, including two that are identical in every column (a conversion that updated through a key or ctid it picked once, or LIMIT 1, would change one), and must not touch sensors whose numbers share digits or sign with 3 (30, -3) or are 0. Those rows hold the same RecordedWhen and Temperature as the sensor-3 rows, so only the sensor number tells them apart.

cases.label: readings for a new sensor interleaved with an existing one: the first inserts, the third updates the row the first inserted, the existing sensor is updated
cases.reasoning: Readings are applied one at a time in SensorDataListID order. Reading 1 (sensor 4, new) inserts; reading 2 updates sensor 5's existing row; reading 3 (sensor 4 again) must find the row reading 1 inserted and update it. A set-based conversion that decided insert-or-update for all readings against the table as it was before the call would insert sensor 4 twice. The hand-derived case sends two consecutive readings for one sensor with no other sensor in between.
